paper_inconsistencies.check: Table 1: white SQ vs NSQ chi2 = 2.56, p = .110; the significant white difference is SQ vs neutral (Table 2, p = .024)
tables: phase 1 SQ vs NSQ red, silver blue and tan negative, SQ vs N red and silver blue negative; phase 2 silver blue SQ vs NSQ and white SQ vs N negative

paper_inconsistencies.printed: chi2 = 3.90, p = .048 with OR 2.33 [0.99, 5.51] and h 0.27 [-0.02, 0.56] (Table 3; text p. 13 calls it significant)
paper_inconsistencies.check: not a contradiction: the Wald OR CI and the normal-approximation h CI use different approximations from the prop.test chi-square, so they can include the null at p = .048; the text's 'significant' follows the printed p (rmd2 computes all three)
